stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $X$ be a Hausdorff quasi-compact topological space and $\mathcal F$ an abelian sheaf. Define $\check H^n(X,\mathcal F)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal U}\check H^n(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ over all open coverings ordered by refinement. For every $n$ the canonical comparison $\check H^n(X,\mathcal F)\to H^n(X,\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
hypotheses:
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff and quasi-compact topological space. Let
$\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $X$.
conclusions:
Then
the map $\check{H}^n(X, \mathcal{F}) \to H^n(X, \mathcal{F})$ defined
in (\ref{equation-cech-to-cohomology}) is an isomorphism for
all $n$.

reason: Gives extensive refinement-based universal delta functor argument, but explicitly omits multiple independence/additivity checks and has repeated F in the printed three-column diagram.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
\begin{reference}
\cite[Expose V bis, 4.1.3]{SGA4}
\end{reference}
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $Z \subset X$ be a quasi-compact subset
such that any two points of $Z$ have disjoint open neighbourhoods in $X$.
For every abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ the canonical
map
$$
\colim H^p(U, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
H^p(Z, \mathcal{F}|_Z)
$$
where the colimit is over open neighbourhoods $U$ of $Z$ in $X$
is an isomorphism.
conclusions:
For every abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ the canonical
map
$$
\colim H^p(U, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
H^p(Z, \mathcal{F}|_Z)
$$
where the colimit is over open neighbourhoods $U$ of $Z$ in $X$
is an isomorphism.

reason: Uses quasi-compact Hausdorff refinement to lift Cech cocycles from closed subset to ambient neighborhoods, but explicitly omits dimension-shifting justification for injective acyclicity.
